beu-campori-gonzaga-1537-c13.summary: A two-section secret Piedmont intelligence sheet copied in Mantua and enclosed in Federico II Gonzaga's 6 May 1537 letter to Ferrante Gonzaga: Section 1 criticises an unnamed figure [46] for reckless, vain conduct and notes that the Bishop of Casale (contextually Bernardino Castellari, called della Barba) is held under suspicion through Speciano (contextually Giovanni Battista Speciano); Section 2 reports troops passing over to {L2?} with banners unfurled, the surrender of the fortress of Hesdin (Edim, 13-14 April 1537), Giovio's (contextually Paolo Giovio's) warning to {L30?}, and public opinion in Milan that {L30?} stands in the worst possible credit. Shown here in the re-check layer (27 Nov 2026): the contributor's transcription with 12 corrections from the Estense scans, viewed by an AI model only; no person has checked the corrected places. The English translation is the contributor's, made from his filed reading.

Conventions: ⟨...⟩ marks inline clear Italian written unenciphered on c. 13r. Square brackets ([...], [?...], [NN]) and {L..?} mirror the same open codes, provisional candidate nulls, contextual readings, and emended passages marked in reading13r13v.md. Glosses in parentheses after historical titles or surnames — e.g. (i.e., Bernardino Castellari, called Bernardino della Barba) — are editorial historical identifications of the shorter manuscript references (il vescovo de Casale, el Speciano, Il Iovio), not words decoded from the cipher.

To [?Fasgnino].

⟨So that you may understand that I have not spoken above without reason:⟩ [23] [46] is the [most] reckless ⟨and⟩ the [most] [?unprincipled] man ⟨in the⟩ world: whoever tried to ⟨pull⟩ [him taut] would snap him, not [27] ⟨considering⟩ who {L2?} is and who {L30?} is;
